primaryKeyword: what is the lowest price of seo
h1: The lowest price of SEO, and the arithmetic that kills it
metaTitle: What Is the Lowest Price of SEO? The Floor, in INR
metaDescription: The lowest price of SEO in India is about ₹2,999 a month. We run the unit maths on that number and show how few hours of real work it can actually fund.
answer: The lowest advertised price for SEO in India is about ₹2,999 a month. At a junior executive's fully loaded cost of roughly ₹350 an hour, that's 8.5 hours before overhead and closer to 5 after it. The work in those packages honestly needs 30 to 55 hours. The gap is filled with automation.
takeaways: ₹2,999 buys about **five delivered hours a month**. The line items in the same proposal need thirty to fifty-five.
The one item they can genuinely afford to deliver is directory and bookmark submissions — which is also the one item that can actively damage your site.
Cheap SEO isn't usually a scam. It's arithmetic nobody says out loud, dressed as a package.
The honest floor for work that changes anything is **₹40,000 a month** for a small site. Below that, do it yourself and do less of it.

body: Search for cheap SEO in India and the same shape of offer appears everywhere: ₹2,999, ₹4,999 or ₹7,999 a month, listed as a Basic / Standard / Premium ladder, with a tick-list of eight to twelve deliverables per tier. Usually a six or twelve month minimum. Usually a promise about keywords ranking on page one.
Nobody is lying about the price. ₹2,999 really is what you'll be invoiced. The interesting question is what ₹2,999 can physically fund, and that question has an exact answer.
So let's do the division instead of arguing about the vibe.

The cheapest person who can legitimately touch an SEO account in India is a junior executive. Salary ₹20,000–₹28,000 a month. Load that with PF, insurance, a laptop, a seat and the fact that nobody produces work for every hour they're at a desk, and the real cost lands between **₹280 and ₹380 per productive hour**. Call it ₹350 and be generous about it.
₹2,999 ÷ ₹350 = **8.5 hours a month**. That's the ceiling, and it assumes every rupee becomes labour.

It doesn't. A package sold at this price has to fund a sales function, a marketplace listing or ad spend to acquire you, software, and some margin. That's realistically 35–40% of the invoice, which leaves **about five delivered hours a month**. Roughly one hour a week.
One hour a week is enough to run an automated report and paste the output into a template. It is not enough to open your site.

callout.title: ₹350 is a cost, not a rate
callout.body: This is what the agency pays to have a junior exist for an hour — not what they'd bill you. Every number on this page is calculated in their favour. If anything, real delivered hours at ₹2,999 are under five, because a junior handling forty accounts spends a large part of the day switching between them.

sections.h2: What's in the package, line by line, against what it actually takes
body: Here's the standard deliverables list from a sub-₹3,000 package, with the honest time each line needs from someone competent, and what five hours can realistically produce instead.

table.caption: A ₹2,999 SEO package: promised line items versus the hours the work honestly needs.
head: Advertised line item
Hours to do it properly
What ₹2,999 actually produces
rows: A list exported from one free tool. Nobody checked search intent, competition, or whether you already rank.
Title tags and meta descriptions regenerated by a plugin, keyword inserted at the front.
A crawl report emailed to you, with the implementation left to your developer. That's a diagnosis, not a fix.
Two 400–600 word posts, generated or spun, unedited, published on a blog nobody links to.
Genuinely delivered. It's the only affordable item on the list — and the only one that can hurt you.
An automated fourteen-page PDF, mostly screenshots, tracking keywords chosen because you were already close on them.

bullets: The shortfall isn't 20%. It's roughly **six to eleven times**. No amount of efficiency, offshoring or AI drafting closes a gap that size while the output still has to be read by a human buyer.
Notice which item survives the squeeze. The cheapest deliverable to automate is the one that gets delivered in volume — and it happens to be the one with a downside.

sections.h2: Submissions and network links: the deliverable that costs you later
body: Directory blasts, bookmark submissions, article-directory posts and links from a vendor's own network of blogs are cheap because they're automated and because nobody wants them. That's the same reason they don't work.

Google has spent two decades getting better at recognising link patterns that were placed rather than earned. A sudden run of 200 links from unrelated low-quality directories, all with your target keyword as the anchor text, is not a subtle signal. The best case is that those links are ignored entirely and you paid ₹2,999 a month for nothing. The realistic worse case is a manual action or an algorithmic suppression that takes months of remediation to lift.

The remediation is where the money actually goes. A backlink audit, a disavow file and a few months of monitoring is around ₹45,000 of work — fifteen months of the retainer that caused it. We itemise that whole bill on [the cheapest digital marketing agency](/cost/cheapest-digital-marketing-agency).
Ask any cheap provider one question: **where do the links come from?** "Our network" means a private blog network. "High-DA sites" with no names means the same thing with better vocabulary.

callout.title: Ask before you sign, not after
callout.body: Ask for ten example placements from an existing client. Not domains — actual live URLs. If the answer is a confidentiality clause, that's the answer. Real link builders show their work because it's the hardest thing they do.

sections.h2: The honest floor is ₹40,000, and here's what changes at it
body: There is a real number below which SEO stops being possible, and it isn't a marketing position — it's the point at which the arithmetic above stops failing.

At a blended agency delivery cost near ₹1,200 an hour for a team that mixes senior and junior time, ₹40,000 a month funds roughly 24 delivered hours after tools and overhead. That is enough — just — to actually do the six line items in that table once a month, for a site under about 30 pages, in a market with a few dozen serious competitors. The [full band-by-band breakdown sits here](/cost/seo-agency-cost).

What changes at ₹40,000 isn't volume. It's that a person with judgement looks at your site, decides what the binding constraint is, and spends the whole budget there instead of spreading it across a tick-list. That single decision is most of the value.

₹40,000 is our floor too, for smaller sites. Standard SEO runs from ₹75,000/mo, which is the first level where technical, content, outreach and analysis can all be staffed at once rather than queueing behind one generalist. Both ex-GST, both month-to-month after the first quarter.

sections.h2: If ₹5,000 a month really is your ceiling, do this instead
body: This is a genuine position to be in and it isn't shameful. A new clinic, a single-branch restaurant, a freelancer, a shop — ₹40,000 a month is not available and won't be for a year.
The correct move is not to buy a cheaper version of a programme. It's to do the small number of things that work, yourself, and stop paying anyone. In rough order of return per hour:
numbered: **Finish your Google Business Profile.** Right primary category, every service listed, real photographs, accurate hours, products, and the Q&A section seeded with the questions customers actually ask you on the phone. Free, and for a local business it outperforms every ₹2,999 package ever sold.
**Get twenty real reviews over three months.** Ask in person, at the moment the customer is happiest. Never buy them — bought reviews get removed and the profile gets flagged.

**Write one honest page per service you sell.** 600–900 words, in your own words, answering what it costs, what's included, who it's for and who it isn't. Most small-business sites have one page saying "Services" and that's the whole problem.

**Install Google Search Console and read the query report once a month.** Free. It tells you exactly which searches already find you and which pages are nearly ranking. Twenty minutes a month beats a year of somebody else's PDF.

**Fix the four technical things that matter at your size:** the site loads on HTTPS, it renders properly on a phone, every page has a different title, and a sitemap is submitted. That's an afternoon, once.

**Answer your ten most-asked customer questions on your own site**, one page each, in plain language. This is what AI assistants and featured snippets pull from, and almost nobody in a local market bothers.

**Save the ₹5,000.** Seven months of it buys one real audit — around ₹35,000 — which tells you exactly what to fix and gives you a plan to execute yourself. That's a far better use of ₹35,000 than twelve months of automated reports. [Per-deliverable pricing is broken down here](/cost/seo-services-cost).

callout.title: The uncomfortable summary
callout.body: Under about ₹25,000 a month, doing it yourself badly beats paying someone else to do it badly — because at least you'll know which parts got done, and nobody will be building links you'll have to disavow later.

faqs.q: What is the lowest price of SEO in India?
faqs.a: About ₹2,999 a month for advertised packages, with ₹4,999 and ₹7,999 tiers above it. Those prices are real, but at a junior's fully loaded cost of roughly ₹350 an hour, ₹2,999 funds around five delivered hours a month once sales, tools and margin come out.

faqs.q: Can SEO work for ₹5,000 per month?
faqs.a: Not as an agency service. Five thousand rupees is roughly eight hours of junior time before overhead, and the deliverables in a typical package need thirty-plus. Spent on your own Google Business Profile, reviews and service pages, ₹5,000 of your own time works considerably better.

faqs.q: Why are cheap SEO packages bad if the price is honest?
faqs.a: The price is honest; the deliverables list isn't. It promises thirty to fifty-five hours of work at a price that funds five. The gap gets filled with automation, and the only automated deliverable that scales — bulk directory and network links — is the one that can trigger a penalty.

faqs.q: What is the minimum realistic SEO budget for a small business?
faqs.a: ₹40,000 a month for a site under about 30 pages in a moderately competitive market, ex-GST. That funds roughly 24 delivered hours plus, critically, someone senior deciding where those hours go. Below it, do fewer things yourself rather than more things badly.

faqs.q: Are cheap SEO packages ever worth buying?
faqs.a: Occasionally, if you buy exactly one narrow, finite thing — a Google Business Profile setup, a citation cleanup, a one-off crawl. Those are real jobs with an end. What doesn't work is buying a miniature version of an ongoing four-discipline programme.

faqs.q: How do I check whether a cheap agency is buying bad links?
faqs.a: Ask for ten live example placements from a current client, then open them. Look for pages with unrelated content, dozens of outbound links, no real traffic, and thin site-wide quality. Also check your own referring domains in Search Console monthly — a sudden spike is the tell.
